text:
alana: FYI CI microbench for PR #11523 just crossed the performance threshold on the kernel-selector test. failing diff is +11.8% tail latency on the small-seqlen path.

mike: ugh, which bench exactly?

alana: kernel_selector_micro.py -> test_kv_cache_warmup_latency. CI log: `median 2.9ms -> 3.3ms`, `p95 6.2ms -> 6.9ms`, tail shows the biggest shift. Attached excerpt below.

perf-bot: [CI] kernel_selector_micro.py: threshold diff exceeded (+11.8%). See: https://ci.redwood.internal/runs/8675309

sam: Can you paste the failing golden diff?

alana: sure:
```
--- baseline
+++ pr
@@
 p95: 6.2ms -> 6.9ms (+11.29%)
 p99: 12.5ms -> 13.9ms (+11.2%)
 avg: 3.4ms -> 3.6ms (+5.8%)
```

jen: That pattern (p95/p99 shift with small avg change) smells like batching timing jitter or a KV hit-rate regression. Any change to kv cache or batch timer in the PR?

alana: PR changes: small tweak to kernel autoselect scoring (prefer fp16 kernel for 128-seqlen by 0.5 score) + slight adjustment to batch coalescing window for the low-latency sampler. No direct kv code.

mike: autoselect tweaks could change kernel ordering, which changes warmup behavior and KV lifetime pressure (different cache footprint). Could be a path where a different kernel increases early token time -> delays next batch.

sam: running a local microbench now to reproduce. quick command: `./tools/bench --test kernel_selector_micro.py --runs 1000 --seed 42`

perf-bot: queued repro job on perf-n1. Link: https://perf.redwood.internal/job/1234

sam: repro on my laptop shows a smaller delta (~4%) but CI is noisier. Trying a bisect across commits in the PR.

alana: interestingly CI histogram shows two modes in latency; the higher mode lines up with requests that hit a kernel variant that falls back to slower matmul path. Might be a kernel codegen fallback.

jen: can you dump kernel selection trace? add `--debug kernel-selector` to the bench run. we need to see which kernel id is chosen for those slow requests.

sam: pasted trace snippet:
```
[2026-03-12T14:02:33Z] request id=abc123 seq=32 chosen_kernel=matmul_slow_v2 reason=autoselect_score
[2026-03-12T14:02:33Z] request id=abc124 seq=32 chosen_kernel=fused_gemm_v1 reason=autoselect_tie_break
[2026-03-12T14:02:33Z] request id=abc125 seq=32 chosen_kernel=matmul_fast_v1 reason=cache_affinity
```

mike: aha — occasional matmul_slow_v2. That wasn't common before. Which commit introduced matmul_slow_v2 exposure?

sam: bisect narrowed it to commit 8f7c9a (the autoselect score change). Reverting that single line locally brings p95 back down.

alana: If revert repros, we should either revert the autoselect tweak on PR or adjust scoring to prefer stable kernels under low-latency SLO.

jen: also confirm KV hit-rate around those requests. If kernel choice changes memory access pattern, it could evict hot KV entries more often. Can you capture `kv.hits` counters in the same run?

sam: added counters, here's a quick summary (baseline vs pr):
- kv_hit_rate: 92.1% -> 89.3%
- avg_kv_latency: 0.42ms -> 0.56ms

mike: that's significant. A drop in kv hit rate aligns with higher tail. Some requests likely miss and force recompute or slower kernel paths.

alana: Given this is a PR-level regression and CI flagged it, I'd prefer a temporary revert of the autoselect change until we have a patch that maintains kv affinity. Can we cut a revert commit and rerun CI?

jen: +1 for revert as rollout blocker. We should file a followup ticket to refine scoring: prefer kernel variants with stronger cache affinity when SLO prioritized, maybe add a stability hysteresis.

sam: starting revert branch now: `git revert -n 8f7c9a && git commit -m "revert: relax kernel autoselect tweak causing kv warmup regress"`

perf-bot: [CI] queued build for revert branch -> job 8675310

mike: also add a short unit test that asserts kv_hit_rate delta < 1.5% for the microbench; that will catch similar regressions early.

alana: Agreed. I'll open the ticket for hysteresis and add a test case in the PR once revert lands.

sam: CI for revert passed and threshold diff is now -0.3%. Reverting blocked the regression.

alana: Thanks team. Action items: 1) merge revert (done), 2) followup ticket to adjust autoselect to account for kv affinity + hysteresis (OPEN-2312), 3) add microbench kv_hit_rate assertion in CI.

mike: add note to release notes that we reverted an autoselect perf tweak pending stability fixes.

perf-bot: incident created: PERF-ROLLBACK-11523, assigned to eng-runtime.

alan a: :thumbsup:

jen: can we also add a nightly job that runs the microbench under different seeds to surface bimodal tails? Might have caught this sooner.

alana: good idea — I'll schedule a perf-nightly job after the revert.

sam: closing loop; leaving the bench artifacts and kernel traces in the perf job artifacts bucket: s3://perf-artifacts/11523/

mike: good work everyone.
